rundown: Trail Blazers beat Kings 120-107 at Golden 1 Center in Sacramento, CA in front of 14,831. Trail Blazers led 64-53 at the half and never looked back. The 1st quarter decided it: Trail Blazers won it 34-25. By ESPN's win probability it was never really in doubt (never below 74%).
Leading the way — Trail Blazers: Deni Avdija 34 pts; Damian Lillard 6 ast; Donovan Clingan 11 reb. Kings: De'Andre Hunter 24 pts; Darius Acuff Jr. 6 ast; Domantas Sabonis 12 reb.
Where Trail Blazers won it: they shot 48% to 45%, shot 40% from three to 32% and won the boards 41-38.
Against the closing line (DraftKings): Trail Blazers closed as 10.5-point favorites and covered by 2.5; the total closed at 229.5 and they combined for 227, under by 2.5.

review.title: The algo's call
review.body:
Logged before the start, last snapshot Nov 13, 9:58 PM ET. It had Trail Blazers 82% and Kings 18%, projecting Trail Blazers 119.6 – Kings 108.8 (228.4 total, Trail Blazers by 10.8).

Final: Trail Blazers 120 – Kings 107. Right winner: it had Trail Blazers at 82%.

review.title: How the ratings held up
review.body:
Trail Blazers came in with a 2% above average attack and a league-average defense (8-3, 119.5 scored and 112.3 allowed a game over 11 games), worth about 72 and 73 games of evidence. Projected to score 119.6, they scored 120 (+0.4 points, 0% over); projected to allow 108.8, they allowed 107 (−1.8 points, 2% under).

Kings came in with a 3% below average attack and a 5% leakier than average defense (1-10, 108.3 scored and 121 allowed a game over 11 games), worth about 67 and 67 games of evidence. Projected to score 108.8, they scored 107 (−1.8 points, 2% under); projected to allow 119.6, they allowed 120 (+0.4 points, 0% over).

The bigger miss was Kings' scoring (-1.8 points against projection).
